cues.title: The Curtain Opens

hook.recognition: A4–B4–D5, then B4–A4; the following F#4–A4–B4–A4 answer
hook.preserve: Current principal hook pitches and recognizable refrain; no borrowed reference melody.

sources.program_path: $World Suite 3.ufs/Presets/01 Types/Metal & Gong/Steel Pan/Steel Pan Main.uvip

performers.purpose: One principal steel-pan melody, with complete statements and deliberate rests.
performers.reference_principle: Andy Narell: lyrical pan/band interaction; Greenidge and Provost: phrase-shaped roll studies.
performers.performance: Retain the current C1 hook. Shape single-strike attacks and releases; reserve alternating-hand double-time rolls for selected sustained cadences, not every long note. Vary stroke emphasis and check repeated-sample artifacts.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Keep the source maximizer bypassed and generous transient headroom. Review upper-mid pan edge against the actual mix before further cuts.

performers.purpose: Warm offbeat chords and a written answer; foreground dialogue only when pan rests.
performers.reference_principle: Nocentelli: economical interlocking cell; Ranglin: warm complementary chord/lead vocabulary.
performers.performance: Use playable small voicings and believable staggered strokes. Leave the pan phrase ending open; change comping density between verse and refrain.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Harmonic movement and a complete bridge phrase derived from the established hook.
performers.reference_principle: Monty Alexander: responsive trio conversation; Bonobo: a recognizable phrase survives changes in layers.
performers.performance: Use mid-register voicings, fewer sustained tones under the pan, and a written bridge statement rather than ongoing fills.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared. Produced layers are declared overdubs; one physical keyboard/guitar never comps and plays its lead simultaneously.
performers.tone_review: The EP audition loses about 4.84 dB RMS on mono fold-down. Essential harmony must survive mono; adjust spatial processing or choose a safer voicing/source after comparison.

performers.purpose: A memorable two-bar bass relationship supporting the chorus and percussion.
performers.reference_principle: George Porter Jr.: economical bass/guitar/drum interaction.
performers.performance: Control attack and note endings, anchor the harmonic arrivals, and use one explicit turnaround instead of a fill every bar.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Congas lead the living rhythm; maraca is an alternative texture.
performers.reference_principle: Mongo Santamaria: conga articulation and ensemble conversation.
performers.performance: Distinguish open, closed, slap and quiet connecting strokes where supported. Write one identifiable cycle and meaningful phrase variants.
performers.physical_model: Congas and maracas alternate in the live model; any simultaneous shaker pass is a declared studio overdub.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: A compact warm electronic anchor and controlled transitions, supporting the hand drums.
performers.reference_principle: Bonobo: deliberate bass/percussion relationships and entries/withdrawals; Cirrus is a repeated-figure study.
performers.performance: Use selected rounded kick/rim/hat events and change density by section. No continuous eight-layer beat; no automatic hiss or bit reduction.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared. Produced layers are declared overdubs; one physical keyboard/guitar never comps and plays its lead simultaneously.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: A separate player supplies short timbales/bell punctuation in chosen refrains.
performers.reference_principle: Willie Bobo: a distinct timbales role alongside Mongo’s congas.
performers.performance: Reserve bell time and fills for named passages; leave space at the principal melody entrance.
performers.physical_model: Separate guest from conga player; timbales and bell share a plausible two-stick setup.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

sections.name: Curtain hook
sections.development: State a short recognizable pan opening with bass; do not start with a long percussion intro.
sections.handoff: Pan completes its pickup; congas enter at the verse.

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.development: Two written eight-bar sentences: plain theme, then a guitar/conga answer. Keys and guest rest.
sections.handoff: Leave the final phrase ending open for the pre-chorus.

sections.name: Pre-chorus 1
sections.development: Harmonic lift and reduced percussion make the chorus arrival clear.
sections.handoff: Keys release before the pan refrain; no overlapping fill.

sections.name: Chorus 1
sections.development: Full hook, wider chord body and a clear bass answer; preserve a single foreground.
sections.handoff: Reduce the producer layer and keys before Verse 2.

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.development: Change bass movement and exchange the answer between guitar and keys. The electronic kit rests.
sections.handoff: A short conga punctuation leads to the lift.

sections.name: Pre-chorus 2
sections.development: Repeat the recognizable lift with a different register and more space.
sections.handoff: Pan returns clearly on the next downbeat.

sections.name: Chorus 2
sections.development: Guest timbales supplies one written response; remove another subdivision so the song does not simply become louder.
sections.handoff: Pan finishes and rests for the bridge.

sections.name: Keys bridge
sections.development: A complete quieter keyboard sentence uses established material. Hand drums and pan rest.
sections.handoff: Keys end the sentence; guitar receives the next foreground.

sections.name: Band dialogue
sections.development: Guitar carries a written answer; pan returns only in its reserved reply. No open-ended solo.
sections.handoff: A clear cadence and short rest announce the final hook.

sections.name: Final chorus
sections.development: First eight bars state the hook plainly; the second eight develop response/register and a selected shaped pan roll.
sections.handoff: Thin the accompaniment before the final phrase resolves.

sections.name: Curtain close
sections.development: A written cadence and natural ring end the song.
sections.handoff: All rhythmic layers stop intentionally; preserve the tail.

references: Harry Belafonte — Jump in the Line: revue/call-and-response formal context
DKC1 — DK Island Swing: contrasting episodes and a strong return
Andy Narell — Coffee Street: pan/band phrasing
cues.proposed_change: Replace the meandering C1/verse/C2 chain with clearly named verse, preparation, chorus, bridge and written dialogue. One pan, more harmonic/rhythmic weight elsewhere.

cues.title: Cloudwater Crossing

hook.preserve: Current flute pitch contour and refrain; slower proposed tempo and clearer breaths require review.

performers.purpose: Principal flute hook and expressive, breathable statements.
performers.reference_principle: Herbie Mann: clear flute phrasing over groove; DKC Aquatic Ambience: spacious scene identity.
performers.performance: Retain G4–D5–E5–D5–B4 recognition, its answering phrase and breathing points. Shape dynamics rather than keeping every attack equally strong.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Sparse harmonic color; a feature only in the reduced bridge.
performers.reference_principle: Bonobo Break Apart: stages of harmonic/rhythmic development; Monty: purposeful voicing.
performers.performance: Hold fewer chord tones, change register at the bridge, and release before flute returns.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Keep essential harmonic information audible in mono; the tested EP spatial setting needs a mono comparison before full construction.

performers.purpose: A buoyant recurring bass figure with space.
performers.reference_principle: George Porter: relationship rather than constant doubling.
performers.performance: Use short and sustained notes intentionally; let the lower tabla/udu resonance finish.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Valiha ostinato and one complete plucked dialogue, using the guest’s separate related-string study lane.
performers.reference_principle: The plucked guest contributes counterpoint; Valiha requires its own technique study rather than being called a kora performance.
performers.performance: Use the verified Valiha D1 selector 3. Separate accompaniment and foreground registers; a two-hand plucked figure remains readable.
performers.physical_model: One selected Valiha performance. Kora is not simultaneously added; it remains a separate auditioned option.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Tabla leads selected rhythmic sections; udu provides a contrasting spacious bridge.
performers.reference_principle: Zakir Hussain: articulated ensemble dialogue; the udu needs its own touch, not a transferred tabla pattern.
performers.performance: Modern Tabla note48 is a low tone, note60 a G-labelled stroke and note55 a D-labelled stroke. Verify sounding tuning against G major. Write rests and phrase variants; udu replaces tabla in the bridge.
performers.physical_model: Tabla and udu alternate complete sections; any simultaneous extra take must be declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Light foley subdivision and original processed-band atmosphere.
performers.reference_principle: Bonobo Kiara/Break Apart: a hook with changing surroundings; acoustic subtraction remains meaningful.
performers.performance: Use the actual Foley kick/wood/shaker map selectively. Texture has a destination and exit; it does not mask the flute or become a permanent backbeat.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared. Produced layers are declared overdubs; one physical keyboard/guitar never comps and plays its lead simultaneously.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: A small number of warm chord answers.
performers.reference_principle: Ranglin/Nocentelli contextual chord placement, adapted to the air/discovery scene.
performers.performance: Use fewer strokes than Opera; guitar rests for most of the airy passages.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

sections.name: Cloudwater opening
sections.development: Valiha opens a short landscape; flute gives a recognizable pickup before the first refrain.
sections.handoff: Valiha reduces to accompaniment when flute enters.

sections.name: Refrain 1
sections.development: State the approved hook clearly with a small tabla conversation and no full kit.
sections.handoff: Flute breath ends before the verse response.

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.development: Reduce to flute, bass and selected warm answers. The tabla and foley layers rest.
sections.handoff: Keys prepare the next four-bar lift.

sections.name: Pre-refrain 1
sections.development: Use harmonic/register lift rather than a loud riser.
sections.handoff: Flute receives the downbeat; keys move behind it.

sections.name: Refrain 2
sections.development: Return the hook with one added harmonic layer and one fewer plucked subdivision.
sections.handoff: Flute completes the phrase and rests.

sections.name: Plucked dialogue
sections.development: A complete Valiha answer develops existing material; no aimless new tune.
sections.handoff: The plucked sentence ends before the next flute entrance.

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.development: A second quiet verse changes register and bass relationship, preserving the hook family.
sections.handoff: A deliberate breath prepares the lift.

sections.name: Pre-refrain 2
sections.development: Recognizable harmonic preparation with a sparse electronic answer.
sections.handoff: Remove the electronic answer before the hook.

sections.name: Refrain 3
sections.development: A confident return; the foley pulse adds motion without an acoustic kit.
sections.handoff: Percussion thins into the udu bridge.

sections.name: Udu bridge
sections.development: Switch from tabla to udu; exposed harmony and atmosphere create real contrast.
sections.handoff: Flute resumes after a complete keyboard phrase and brief space.

sections.name: Final refrain
sections.development: First statement remains plain; second uses a changed plucked answer and register. Keep breaths and foreground intact.
sections.handoff: Remove rhythmic layers in a written order.

sections.name: Sky settle
sections.development: A quiet written cadence preserves air and natural decay.
sections.handoff: Finish with a clear endpoint and tail.

references: Miriam Makeba — Pata Pata: concise recognizable refrain/contrasting episodes
Bonobo — Kiara / Break Apart: foreground identity and staged accompaniment
DKC1 — Aquatic Ambience / Treetop Rock: spacious setting with forward motion
Zakir Hussain — Making Music: specific ensemble/stroke dialogue
cues.proposed_change: Slow the current 112 BPM surface to 100; give tabla/udu different whole-section roles and replace constant kit/guitar coverage with selected entrances. No steel pan.

cues.title: Welcome Home

hook.recognition: Original approved 3/4 theme: D4–C4–Bb3, then F4 into G4; descending home gesture and complete eight-bar answer.
hook.preserve: Return to the original owner-approved 3/4 A/B melody; the later 4/4 warm-ensemble study remains historical.

performers.purpose: Principal warm steel-string guitar home theme.
performers.reference_principle: Ranglin: melodic economy and warm phrasing; Bonobo Black Sands: a three-beat landscape and growing return.
performers.performance: Keep the current theme’s pitch contour; propose a 3/4 phrasing adaptation for owner review. Use playable positions, soft attacks and intentional releases.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Sunbird is steel-string. Retain warmth through touch and the tested corrective EQ, not by relabelling it nylon or removing all articulation.

performers.purpose: Selected nylon chord support and an answering phrase.
performers.reference_principle: Nocentelli/Ranglin: complementary rhythmic voicings rather than constant full strumming.
performers.performance: Use small chord shapes; withdraw when piano supplies full harmony. No continuous two-guitar blanket.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Key Suite Acoustic TDR Mellow Dark supplies warm chord body, a distinct piano bridge and an answering phrase.
performers.reference_principle: Monty: lyrical/harmonic contribution; Bonobo: acoustic development and meaningful subtraction.
performers.performance: Use the tested piano voice in a restrained middle register; let releases and a complete phrase distinguish the bridge.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared. Produced layers are declared overdubs; one physical keyboard/guitar never comps and plays its lead simultaneously.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

sources.program_path: $Jazzistic.ufs/Presets/03 Instruments/02 Jazz Double Bass/Jazzistic Double Bass.M5p

performers.purpose: Upright bass anchors the home pulse and adds a short returning answer.
performers.reference_principle: John Clayton contextual acoustic ensemble study, alongside Porter’s economy.
performers.performance: Let note endings support the proposed waltz. Do not automatically walk continuously or double every guitar attack.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Discrete brush/rim support in selected returns.
performers.reference_principle: Jeff Hamilton: serving the phrase, with brush technique distinct from sticks.
performers.performance: Use only supported discrete brush articulations initially; continuous sweeps are not demonstrated by the current test. Rest during the bodhran-led verses.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: A soft frame-drum conversation gives the verses a wood/skin identity.
performers.reference_principle: John Joe Kelly with Flook: separate body, strokes and ensemble role; no transplanted tabla vocabulary.
performers.performance: Choose documented hit identities by a focused audition, then write a restrained three-beat part. Do not fake continuous hand-pressure pitch movement with an unverified control.
performers.physical_model: One performer on the selected instrument; additional simultaneous studio layers are declared.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

performers.purpose: Subtle original texture, selected wood accents and a warm transition.
performers.reference_principle: Bonobo Black Sands/Polyghost: acoustic center, gradual arrival and useful subtraction.
performers.performance: Use foley only where the physical players leave a space; no permanent kick/snare loop. An original processed guitar/piano tail may answer a phrase.
performers.physical_model: Programmed texture and foley are declared studio parts, distinct from the physical drum players. Produced layers are declared overdubs; one physical keyboard/guitar never comps and plays its lead simultaneously.
performers.tone_review: Choose touch/register and balance first; review EQ at matched level, mono and speech space.

sections.name: Home threshold
sections.development: Introduce the guitar contour immediately; piano gives only a small harmonic frame.
sections.handoff: Guitar continues into the first full refrain.

sections.name: Home refrain 1
sections.development: Plain full melody over a small brush pulse; nylon and producer rest.
sections.handoff: Brushes withdraw for the verse’s frame-drum identity.

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.development: Two written eight-bar sentences, with a lighter second answer. Piano rests so the guitar chords have room.
sections.handoff: The frame drum ends its response before the refrain pickup.

sections.name: Home refrain 2
sections.development: The familiar hook returns with piano body and a restrained electronic tail.
sections.handoff: Guitar finishes and hands the bridge to piano.

sections.name: Piano bridge
sections.development: A complete lyrical keyboard statement with bass; all drum layers rest.
sections.handoff: Piano leaves the next phrase to nylon.

sections.name: Guitar room dialogue
sections.development: A written nylon answer and sparse piano response develop the home material.
sections.handoff: Sunbird returns after the dialogue resolves.

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.development: Change voicing and phrase endings; piano enters only in the second half’s gaps.
sections.handoff: A four-bar preparation thins the texture.

sections.name: Homecoming preparation
sections.development: An intimate harmonic lift preserves the home feeling.
sections.handoff: Piano releases before the guitar hook.

sections.name: Final home refrain
sections.development: First eight bars are familiar; second eight develop the answer and final cadence, with one chord player thinning at each guitar phrase.
sections.handoff: Brushes and electronic accents leave before the coda.

sections.name: Home coda
sections.development: A deliberate resolving phrase, gentle bass ending and natural room decay.
sections.handoff: A completed song ending; a future runtime loop edit is separate.

references: Bonobo — Black Sands: three-beat acoustic development and growing return
DKC1 — Candy’s Love Song / Simian Segue: welcoming, immediately legible home identity
Ernest Ranglin — Surfin’: warm guitar phrasing and complementary chords
Flook / John Joe Kelly: frame-drum interaction; Montreux Alexander: responsive acoustic keys/bass
cues.proposed_change: Private test returns to the original approved 3/4 home theme at 84 BPM. Key Suite Acoustic TDR Mellow Dark is the contrasting second voice; bodhran verses and soft lo-fi kit refrains alternate. No steel pan.
